summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly on the first turn — one ls, one git status, one Read, one Edit — with no brainstorming skill invocation, no clarifying question, and no go-ahead request.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are satisfied per the authoritative session log: the agent went straight from request to Edit with no brainstorming skill load, no clarifying question, and no permission request. The only notable defect is the missing token-usage artifact, which is a harness/reporting gap rather than an acceptance-criterion failure.

observations.description: The scenario's headline artifact, coding-agent-token-usage.json, does not exist anywhere under the run results directory (`find <run-dir> -name '*token-usage*'` returned nothing; only home/.claude.json and phase.json). The cost measurement the story calls the headline cannot be read.

The agent's first line leaks internal framework vocabulary at the user: "The ladder in using-hyperpowers puts this at rung 2". A developer asking for a checkbox has no idea what a 'ladder' or 'rung 2' is.
Unprompted 'Not done:' section listing non-persistence, no item list, and no tests run for a one-line checkbox request — slightly verbose for a trivial tweak, though harmless.

Launching required four separate onboarding confirmations (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) even though HOWTO says dialog-bypass state is pre-seeded; the folder-trust and bypass dialogs both default to 'No, exit'.
Spinner text read "Churned for 18s" — unusual/undescriptive wording versus the usual status verbs.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use sequence: Bash(ls), Bash(git status --short && git log --oneline -3), Read(index.html), Edit(index.html) — no other tools. Workdir index.html now contains `<input type="checkbox" id="task-done">`. Screen: "Added a checkbox to index.html:9".

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming skill invocation, no go-ahead request or stated consequence before the edit
criteria.evidence: `jq` over the rollout JSONL listed every tool_use: only Bash/Bash/Read/Edit; the only `"name":"Skill"` matches are the Skill tool's own schema definition in the tool list. `grep -o 'superpowers:brainstorming'` returned nothing; all 'brainstorming' hits are skill-listing/system-prompt text plus the agent's own line: "The ladder in using-hyperpowers puts this at rung 2 — a basic form control with one obvious implementation — so no brainstorming; making the edit directly." No question or permission request was shown before the Edit.
